strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the 'last-mile gap' in formal mathematics with concrete, compelling examples from practitioners (Tao, Zhang)
Principled modular multi-agent architecture that cleanly factorizes failure modes (semantic plausibility vs. syntactic validity) enabling specialized feedback loops
Comprehensive rigorous evaluation: 4,028 type-checked instances, 8 diverse models, human provability audit (78% validity on 138 sampled instances providing independent ground truth)
Real-world validation through successful Mathlib merges (3+ lemmas) demonstrates practical utility and community acceptance beyond benchmarking
Excellent reproducibility documentation: complete pseudocode, exact prompt templates with extraction logic, detailed hyperparameters, and artifact structure

Valuable insights on specialist vs. generalist trade-offs (Goedel 29.6% foundational vs. 13.0% abstract), diversity > scale principle (45% collective vs. 22% individual), and reasoning distillation criticality
Addresses benchmark saturation by remaining genuinely challenging (individual 7-22%, collective 45%) while solvable (human 78%), advancing beyond MiniF2F saturation
Produces reusable community assets: 1,812 verified proofs and 4,028-instance benchmark across diverse domains (Foundational/Applied/Abstract)
Methodologically sound conservative filtering minimizing hallucination (54% of Judge-rejected were actually valid), with semantic novelty checking via aesop
weaknesses: Judge Agent has concerning 46% false negative rate—valid mathematical statements are filtered out, potentially excluding legitimate folklore from benchmark
All benchmark construction (discovery and filtering) uses only GPT-5.1 frontier model, creating optimization bias; unclear if diverse models would select equivalent lemmas or if generalization holds
Proof generation success rates are modest: 55% of benchmark has no verified proof (1,216 of 4,028 instances), individual models max 22%, raising questions about practical utility of unproven lemmas

Fundamental limitation identified but unresolved: 68% of audit failures from missing hypotheses (non-emptiness, continuity, etc.)—indicates discovery-stage LLM limitation that downstream agents cannot fix

Semantic novelty verification gap acknowledged by authors: 'syntactic uniqueness may overlook semantically equivalent statements'; triviality filter via aesop is incomplete, risking benchmark pollution
Limited upstreaming evidence: only 3 lemmas explicitly merged (anonymized), described as 'pilot effort' suggesting incomplete validation; could strengthen claims with commit details or PR links

Closed-book evaluation is conservative and conflates reasoning with knowledge recall; real-world usage with Mathlib retrieval would likely yield higher performance, potentially misrepresenting practical utility

Reproducibility dependencies are substantial: requires proprietary GPT-5.1 access, release-candidate Lean server (v4.25.0-rc2), redacted code repository; full pipeline reproduction infeasible for most researchers
No direct comparison with most relevant baselines (LeanConjecturer, Lemmanaid) mentioned in related work; would substantiate superiority claims beyond problem formulation novelty
Critical failure mode (missing hypotheses) relegated to Appendix D; 22% human audit failure rate and 55% unproven instance rate not sufficiently highlighted as limitations in main text

strengths: Well-motivated task (folklore mining) addresses a genuine last-mile gap in formal mathematics with clear practical examples
Sound modular pipeline architecture that elegantly factorizes failure modes (semantic plausibility → syntactic correctness → proof search) with specialized feedback loops
Rigorous validation: Lean kernel verification, 78% human audit of residuals, 84% held-out audit, detailed failure mode analysis, and real-world validation via 3 Mathlib merges
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 models with domain stratification revealing interpretable trade-offs (specialist vs. generalist, domain-specific degradation)
Exceptional reproducibility: complete prompts, hyperparameters, pseudocode, and implementation details enabling community reproduction
Substantial durable artifacts: 4,028 benchmark statements and 1,506 verified proofs represent direct contributions beyond benchmark scores
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging generation-model dependence, Judge false negatives, closed-book constraints, and unresolved missing-hypotheses problem
weaknesses: Generation-model dependence: GPT-5.1 used exclusively for discovery/judging/formalization makes benchmark partially a reflection of GPT-5.1's folklore intuitions rather than model-independent folklore census
Judge Module false negative rate (46% of rejected statements are valid) suggests recall issues; small prompt ablation (Appendix F) showed limited improvement on this critical failure mode
Missing hypotheses dominates unproven residuals (81%) but remains unresolved; models struggle with formal accounting of conditions, suggesting fundamental limitation not addressed by current approach
Limited upstreaming validation: only 6 lemmas submitted, 3 merged (50% acceptance); weak evidence for practical library utility relative to 1,506 verified proofs claimed as contribution
Closed-book evaluation conflates reasoning with recall; real formalization uses library search—results likely represent conservative lower bound and may not reflect practical usage patterns
Extrapolated 86% solvability estimate (37.39% ÷ 78%) is speculative and drawn from selection-biased sample (model-unsolved residuals), though correctly labeled as diagnostic
No ablation on pipeline necessity: unclear if four-stage modular design is essential or if simpler end-to-end approaches would suffice; no comparison to baseline alternatives
Benchmark durability concerns: tied to specific Lean v4.25.0-rc2 and Mathlib revision requiring periodic rechecking; unlike static benchmarks, requires active maintenance
